Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
1 October 2026 .
Brent $ 102.35 + 4.78 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 Yemeni government forces are holding their coastal positions against Houthi advances after Red Sea losses, per Al Jazeera, though this has not been independently confirmed.

02 Reuters reports three tankers were struck by unknown projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, with the attacker unidentified; crude oil exports from the strait have largely returned to pre-war levels, per The Guardian.

03 Brent stood at $102.35, up 4.78% over 24 hours, as of 20:57 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains severely disrupted. IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day, while The Guardian reports crude oil exports from the strait have largely returned to pre-war levels as producers and shippers adapt, though flows of refined products such as diesel remain constrained. Reuters reports three tankers were struck by unknown projectiles in the strait on Tuesday; the attacker has not been identified. Anadolu Ajansı reports one of those tankers caught fire, citing the UK maritime agency, and also reports a supertanker was hit and caught fire near Oman. The September 30 attacks follow the earlier strike on the Cape Dao on September 23, in which an Indian seafarer was killed. Brent stood at $102.35, up 4.78% over 24 hours, as of 20:57 UTC. Iran says reopening the strait hinges on US guarantees to end the war, per Anadolu Ajansı relaying an Iranian claim. Indian oil refiners have shifted strategy and are hiring tankers to transit the strait directly; no major wire in this feed carries it. On the Red Sea front, Al Jazeera reports Yemeni government forces are holding their coastal positions after suffering losses, with air strikes and difficult terrain limiting Houthi advances; this has not been independently confirmed. Thirty-one events were indexed in the past 24 hours. As of 20:50 UTC, 162 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
